newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/All bets off after expiration.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/All bets off after expiration.

text.p: The U.S. stock market could hold a firm bias into Friday's February option expiration, but index options trading suggests some investors are positioning themselves for a decline in March, traders said Wednesday.
One indication of such positioning is that implied volatilities for March options continue to firm in both the puts and the calls.

One broker in Chicago said his model showed volatilities in the out-of-the-money S&P 100 index .OEX calls at around 18, up from around 16.95. They rose to around 21 in the deep out-of-the-money calls, he said.
OEX put volatilities were up to around 20, the broker said.
"Everything in March is a bit higher," he said.
In March S&P 500 stock index options, implied volatilities in the calls were up to around 17 from the mid-15 region, and were up to around 18 in the puts, he added.

"The volatility has been increasing yesterday and today, particularly in the March options," Jack Callahan, an independent market maker in the OEX, said. "That's reflective of the expectations in the marketplace post expiration."

But he said given the market's run to record high territory, extended with Tuesday's late-session surge that took the OEX to an all-time high close of 793.59 and the SPX to 816.29, upside momentum would likely remain intact for the balance of the week.
Some options strategists said this week that the open interest configuration, particularly in the OEX, suggested an upside bias into the expiration.
But steady, if not heavy, selling of out-of-the-money March calls and buying puts suggested to some that investors were getting nervous.

"April and March volatilities are being held up," one trader in the SPX at the Chicago Board Options Exchange said. "I think the market is getting so toppy that you're seeing a lot of bidders coming in for these downside puts.
"I would have to say the way firms are positioning themselves they're looking for a sell-off," he added. "They have sold a lot of calls today."
In the SPX, the biggest volume was in the February 810 and 800 puts, which traded 16,265 and 14,615 contracts, respectively.
But in the March series, the 840 call traded about 4,070 contracts, the 810 call traded 3,400 and the 810 put traded about 3,350.
Traders said a couple of large firms were the main sellers of March out-of-the-money calls. The March 820 call traded about 675 contracts and the March 900 call traded 235.
Callahan said selling of March out-of-the-money calls in the OEX was not heavy, but that the larger-sized orders were on the call side.
By 1110 CST/1710 GMT, the OEX was up 1.76 at 795.35. It traded between 796.02, a new record, and 790.39. ((-- G.Crawford, 312 408 8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
